title: Minimum Number of Food Buckets to Feed the Hamsters
summary: Given a string representing indices with hamsters ('H') or empty spaces ('.'), determine the minimum number of food buckets to place at empty indices so that each hamster has at least one food bucket adjacent to it.
statement: Given a string representing indices with hamsters ('H') or empty spaces ('.'), determine the minimum number of food buckets to place at empty indices so that each hamster has at least one food bucket adjacent to it. Return -1 if it's impossible to feed all hamsters.
constraints: street contains only H for hamster and . for an available bucket position.
Every hamster needs a bucket in an immediately adjacent empty position; one bucket may feed two hamsters.
Return the minimum bucket count or -1 when impossible.
reference_solution:
def minimum_hamster_buckets(street):
    street=list(street);answer=0
    for index,char in enumerate(street):
        if char!='H':continue
        if index>0 and street[index-1]=='B':continue
        if index+1<len(street) and street[index+1]=='.':street[index+1]='B';answer+=1
        elif index>0 and street[index-1]=='.':street[index-1]='B';answer+=1
        else:return -1
    return answer

    for index,char in enumerate(street):
        if char!='H':continue
        if index>0 and street[index-1]=='B':continue
        if index+2<len(street) and street[index+1]=='.':street[index+1]='B';answer+=1
        elif index>0 and street[index-1]=='.':street[index-1]='B';answer+=1

hints: Placing to the right is best because it may also feed the next hamster.
Scan left to right: if no bucket already sits left, place one right when possible, otherwise left, or fail.
Mark placed buckets in a mutable character list so later hamsters can reuse them.
The greedy right placement never harms an earlier hamster and weakly improves options for the future, establishing minimality by exchange.
